headline: Sensex and Nifty Surge on Strong FII Inflows and Lower Crude Oil Prices

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) recorded 17 consecutive days of buying with Rs 1.22 lakh crore inflows in November.
Lower crude oil prices and strong rally in private banks and FMCG stocks fueled market gains.
Indian markets rallied nearly 2%, helping recoup almost all losses seen in 2026.
Bullish technical signals on charts for select auto and index heavyweights supported sentiment.
whatHappening: Sensex surged over 1,500 to 2,000 points while Nifty topped the 25,900 mark.
Financials received the largest share of foreign capital inflows during November.
Rupee strategists project room for the currency to rally before RBI intervention.
Uber appointed former Zomato food delivery CEO Rakesh Ranjan to lead India and South Asia operations.
summary: Indian equity markets experienced a major rally driven by record foreign institutional inflows of Rs 1.22 lakh crore in November. Sensex zoomed over 1,500 points while Nifty crossed 25,900 led by private banks and FMCG stocks. Oil stocks like BPCL and IOC face geopolitical headwinds despite positive analyst coverage.
